<!-- Generated by scripts/sync-docs.mjs from the compiler README. Edit the README, not this file. -->

On Windows, run `mammoth-0.1.0-setup.exe`. A setup window lets you pick the install folder and choose whether to add Mammoth to `PATH`, then shows progress and the commands to try. By default it installs for your user account in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Mammoth`, adds it to `PATH` and lists it under **Settings → Apps**, where you can uninstall it. It includes its own Java runtime, so you don't need Java or Rust, and it doesn't need administrator rights. If you'd rather not run a setup program, unzip `mammoth-0.1.0-windows-x64.zip` and double-click `install.cmd` inside it for the same window, or run `bin\mammoth.exe` straight from the folder. `install.cmd -Quiet` installs from the console without questions.

Open a new terminal after installing, then run a program:

```powershell
mammoth --version
mammoth "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\Mammoth\examples\greet.mam"
```

This compiles and runs the program. The example prints `Hello, Maya!` and `Hello, Sam!` on separate lines.

Mammoth uses the first Java it finds in this order: the folder in `MAMMOTH_JAVA_HOME`, the runtime installed with it, `JAVA_HOME`, then `java` on `PATH`. Set `MAMMOTH_JAVA_HOME` to a JDK to use a different Java, such as Java 21 for Minecraft mods. The bundled runtime has all of Java SE plus a few JDK modules, listed in `installer/windows/package.ps1`.

The installer is for 64-bit Windows only. On other systems, build from source.

## Build from source

With Rust and a Java 17 or later JDK installed, run these commands once in the VS Code PowerShell terminal from the project folder.

```powershell
cargo build --release
$env:Path = "$(Join-Path $PWD 'target\release');$env:Path"
mammoth .\examples\greet.mam
```

Repeat the PATH line in a new terminal.

To make the Windows installer, run `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File installer\windows\package.ps1` with a JDK 17 or later that has `jmods`. It writes the installed folder, the zip and `mammoth-<version>-setup.exe` to `build\dist`. Before zipping, it checks that the packaged compiler can run a program and build a JAR with every other Java hidden.

To keep the generated `Main.class` for later, run `mammoth .\examples\greet.mam .\build`.

Functions can call other functions defined in the same file. Arguments and list items are evaluated from left to right. Loop variables are scoped to the loop body. In text, `{name}` inserts a value, and `{price * 2}` inserts the result of any expression. Write `\{name}` to print the braces and name literally. Lines beginning with `//` and trailing `//` comments are supported.

Run `cargo test --release` to compile every program under `tests/` and `examples/`, check the bytecode with the JVM's strict verifier, and compare each program's output with its expected `.out` file.
